title: Functor and transformation descent for unnormalized directed stage pairs
statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty directed preorder in any universe, and let $S=(C_i,T_{ij},a^C_{ijk})$ and $S'=(D_i,U_{ij},a^D_{ijk})$ be stage systems [def-sf-directed-common-stage-data]. Object, morphism and index universes may be independent. Their pair categories $P_C,P_D$ and inclusions $j_i^C,j_i^D$ are those of that definition; neither $T_{ii}$ nor $U_{ii}$ is required to be the identity. Suppose functors $\Phi_i:C_i\to D_i$ and natural isomorphisms $b_{ij}:U_{ij}\Phi_i\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_jT_{ij}$ are given for $i\le j$, satisfying, for $i\le j\le k$ and $x\in C_i$,
$$b_{ik,x}\circ a^D_{ijk,\Phi_ix}=\Phi_k(a^C_{ijk,x})\circ b_{jk,T_{ij}x}\circ U_{jk}(b_{ij,x}).$$
No extra unit constraint on $b_{ii}$ is imposed. The formulas
$$\overline\Phi(i,x)=(i,\Phi_ix),\qquad \overline\Phi[m,u]=[m,b_{jm,y}^{-1}\circ\Phi_m(u)\circ b_{im,x}]$$
define a functor $\overline\Phi:P_C\to P_D$. Its representative formula commutes with further stage transport. It satisfies $\overline\Phi j_i^C=j_i^D\Phi_i$ on objects and morphisms, so the corresponding inclusion comparison has identity components.

If $(\Psi_i,c_{ij})$ is another such family and natural transformations $\eta_i:\Phi_i\Rightarrow\Psi_i$ satisfy
$$\eta_{j,T_{ij}x}\circ b_{ij,x}=c_{ij,x}\circ U_{ij}(\eta_{i,x}),$$
then $\overline\eta_{(i,x)}=j_i^D(\eta_{i,x})$ defines a natural transformation $\overline\Phi\Rightarrow\overline\Psi$. A compatible family of isomorphisms descends to an isomorphism. Identity families descend to the identity functor, and composite families descend to composite functors, on objects and morphisms. Identity and vertical composition of transformations descend to identity and vertical composition; whiskering has the corresponding componentwise values. Consequently equations of compatible transformations, including equations involving composition of families, hold after descent.

proof.text:
Let $(\Xi_i,d_{ij}):D\to B$ be coherent, with transitions $V_{ij}$ in $B$. By [lem-pur-associative-stage-family-descent], the composite comparisons are $e^\Phi_{ij}=\Xi_j(b_{ij})d_{ij,\Phi_i}$ and $e^\Psi_{ij}=\Xi_j(c_{ij})d_{ij,\Psi_i}$. Compatibility of $\eta$ and naturality of $d_{ij}$ give
$$\Xi_j(\eta_jT_{ij})e^\Phi_{ij}=\Xi_j(c_{ij})\Xi_jU_{ij}(\eta_i)d_{ij,\Phi_i}=e^\Psi_{ij}V_{ij}(\Xi_i\eta_i).$$
Thus $\Xi_i\eta_i$ descends. Its component is $j_i^B(\Xi_i\eta_{i,x})=\overline\Xi(j_i^D\eta_{i,x})$, using the cited theorem's equality on stage arrows. These are exactly the post-whiskering components. In Lean construct the Hom with τ_i = Functor.whiskerRight (η.τ i) (K.Φ i). Expand comp_β_hom_app, rewrite by naturality of (K.β h).hom at η_i,x, combine the two K_j images with map_comp, and apply η.comm. Its descended component is the reverse of K.functor_map_ι at η_i,x.

proof.text:
For pre-whiskering let $(H_i,h_{ij}):A\to C$ be coherent, with transitions $R_{ij}$ and $h_{ij}:T_{ij}H_i\cong H_jR_{ij}$. The composite comparisons of [lem-pur-associative-stage-family-descent] are $\Phi_j(h_{ij})b_{ij,H_i}$ and $\Psi_j(h_{ij})c_{ij,H_i}$. Naturality of $\eta_j$ at $h_{ij}$ and its compatibility give
$$\eta_{j,H_jR_{ij}}\Phi_j(h_{ij})b_{ij,H_i}=\Psi_j(h_{ij})\eta_{j,T_{ij}H_i}b_{ij,H_i}=\Psi_j(h_{ij})c_{ij,H_i}U_{ij}(\eta_{i,H_i}).$$
Hence $\eta_iH_i$ descends with component $j_i^D(\eta_{i,H_i z})=\overline\eta_{\overline H(i,z)}$, the required pre-whiskering component. In Lean construct the Hom with τ_i = Functor.whiskerLeft (H.Φ i) (η.τ i). Expand comp_β_hom_app, apply η.comm at H_i(x), and rewrite backwards by naturality of η_j at (H.β h).hom.app x. The descended component equality is definitional.

proof.text: Each equality of compatible transformation families is equality of their components. Applying $j_i$ preserves those equalities. The component formula of [lem-pur-associative-stage-family-descent], its identity and vertical-composition laws, and the two whiskering calculations above therefore preserve every asserted equation, including those involving composite families. Equality on all objects is equality of natural transformations. In Lean use NatTrans.ext and funext on X, then congrArg of τ ↦ (T.ι X.stage).map (τ.app X.obj) on the given equality at X.stage. The identity and composite arrow formulas and descended identity/vertical composition are precisely functor_id_map, functor_comp_map, descNatTrans_id and descNatTrans_comp in the cited declaration family.
